title: Vanishing of relative differentials detected on ordinary algebra fibres
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and assume that $A$ is generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra. For each prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $C_{\mathfrak p}=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with its natural $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra structure, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and the fibre ring are as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose $\Omega_{C_{\mathfrak p}/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$ for every $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $M=\Omega_{A/R}$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, with $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$, one has $$M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak q)=0,\qquad M_{\mathfrak q}=0.$$ Here tensor product is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $M_{\mathfrak q}=(A\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}M$ is module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Consequently $\Omega_{A/R}=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00UV (lemma-unramified), proof of (7)--(9) and (11), differential vanishing argument; Lemma Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); Lemma Tag 00RZ (lemma-differentials-finitely-generated); Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK). Applied in Morphisms Lemma Tag 02G8(2), literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A/R$. In the symbol-and-relations construction of $M=\Omega_{A/R}$, the symbols $db$ generate. Additivity and Leibniz give $d(a_1^{e_1}\cdots a_n^{e_n})=\sum_i e_i a_1^{e_1}\cdots a_i^{e_i-1}\cdots a_n^{e_n}\,da_i$ (omit terms with $e_i=0$), and $d(r)=0$ for $r\in R$. Every $b\in A$ is a polynomial in the generators, so every $db$ is an $A$-linear combination of the $da_i$. Thus these finitely many elements generate $M$. This also handles $n=0$, when $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 00RZ (lemma-differentials-finitely-generated), with its elementary generator argument written out; defining derivation relations

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $L=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $C=A\otimes_R k$. The inverse image is prime: $\varphi(xy)\in\mathfrak q$ implies one factor lies in $\mathfrak q$, and $1$ does not. For $s\notin\mathfrak p$, its image in $L$ is nonzero and hence invertible. Thus $r/s\mapsto\overline{\varphi(r)}/\overline{\varphi(s)}$ defines a map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to L$, respecting the fraction relation and killing $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$. It induces $k\to L$. Consequently $\epsilon:C\to L$, $a\otimes t\mapsto\bar a\,\bar t$, is a ring map agreeing with $A\to L$. Its additivity, multiplicativity and balancing follow by multiplication in $L$.

source.place: Tag 00UV (lemma-unramified), proof of (8)--(9): residue-field maps for a prime above its contraction; fraction construction

proof.text: Apply differential base change to $R\to k$ and $R\to A$. Its $C$-linear clause, after interchanging the two tensor factors in the fibre ring, gives $C\otimes_A M\cong\Omega_{C/k}$, with $c\otimes da\mapsto c\,d(a\otimes1)$. The fibre hypothesis therefore implies $C\otimes_A M=0$. The factor interchange is $t\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes t$ and is its own inverse; its multiplicativity follows on pure tensors.

Using $\epsilon$, the maps $M\otimes_A L\to(C\otimes_A M)\otimes_C L$, $m\otimes z\mapsto(1\otimes m)\otimes z$, and $(c\otimes m)\otimes z\mapsto m\otimes\epsilon(c)z$ are inverse $L$-linear maps. The $A$-balancing uses $c\otimes am=(ca)\otimes m$ and the agreement of $A\to C\to L$ with $A\to L$; the outer $C$-balancing uses $\epsilon(cd)=\epsilon(c)\epsilon(d)$. Both composites are identities on the pure tensors, which generate. Since $C\otimes_A M=0$, its tensor product is zero (each pure tensor has zero first factor). Hence $M\otimes_A L=0$.

source.place: Tag 00UV (lemma-unramified), proof of (8)--(9), canonical vector-space identification; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property

proof.text: Put $B=A_{\mathfrak q}$ and $N=M_{\mathfrak q}$. The fractions $(da_i)/1$ generate $N$ over $B$: if $m=\sum_i b_i da_i$, then $m/s=\sum_i(b_i/s)((da_i)/1)$. There is an isomorphism $N\otimes_B L\cong M\otimes_A L$ defined by $(m/s)\otimes z\mapsto m\otimes\bar s^{-1}z$, inverse $m\otimes z\mapsto(m/1)\otimes z$. For well-definedness, equality $m/s=m'/s'$ gives $u(s'm-sm')=0$ with $u,s,s'\notin\mathfrak q$; tensoring this relation and dividing by their nonzero images in $L$ gives the required equality. Balancing by $a/t\in B$ holds since both images are $m\otimes\bar a\bar t^{-1}\bar s^{-1}z$. The composites are identities on pure tensors, since $m/s=s^{-1}(m/1)$. Thus $N$ is finite and $L\otimes_B N=0$, also using the symmetry $n\otimes z\mapsto z\otimes n$.

The ring $B=A_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with residue field $L$. Apply the tensor formulation of the local-generator Nakayama lemma to the finite $B$-module $N$ and the empty family of generators. That family generates $L\otimes_B N=0$, hence generates $N$ itself. The span of the empty family is zero, so $M_{\mathfrak q}=N=0$. All primes $\mathfrak q$ were arbitrary.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (8), empty family; Tag 00UV (lemma-unramified), proof of (7)

proof.text: Finally apply the local-to-global bijectivity criterion to the zero homomorphism $M\to0$. At each maximal ideal its localization is the map $0\to0$, hence bijective, since maximal ideals are prime and the preceding step gives $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$ at every prime. The criterion makes $M\to0$ bijective, so $M=0$. This proves the global conclusion as well as both primewise vanishing assertions. If $A$ is the zero ring there are no primes, and every unital $A$-module is already zero; the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 00UV (lemma-unramified), global differential vanishing argument; local-to-global module criterion Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local, part (6))
